findings.reason: the census missed the owner, so the node as written rebuilds `FilePath` instead of extending it, and the author needs this fact before releasing the node.
findings.text: §5 adds a `nova.paths` resolver and a receipt-root resolver without citing `nova/database/filepath.py` (`FilePath`, `_resolve_absolute` over appdirs) or `nova/definitions.py` (`root_dir`), which already own path resolution; a new subsystem is being proposed where an existing one was never searched for

findings.reason: the node should be decomposed into extensions of the owners it names rather than shipped as one basket of parallel helpers.
findings.text: `replan-small-primitives` gathers a uniform-axis validator, a read-only array constructor, an atomic receipt writer, a trimmed-string check and a canonical digest into one node; these are five shallow wrappers over three unrelated machinery families (`map_extraction`/`diiid_efit`/`mast_efit`, the receipt writers, `machine_evidence`), so the node adds public surface without adding depth

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend the existing mechanism, and without the justification the node forks it.
findings.text: the node states "one trimmed-string check beside `require_string`" and "one canonical digest beside `canonical_json`"; both `require_string` and `canonical_json` exist at `nova/imas/machine_evidence.py:33,64:` and the node gives no reason they cannot be extended (e.g. `require_string(value, context, error, strip=True)`) instead of a parallel function added beside them

findings.reason: a forked resolver and a forked atomic writer drift from the owners the census already shipped an atomic-writer ancestor for, and naming the owner is exactly what this node omits.
findings.text: §5 `replan-gpfs-data-root` proposes "one resolver module (e.g. `nova.paths`) owns the data roots"; the owner to extend is `nova/database/filepath.py` (`FilePath`, which already resolves roots and appdirs) with the base literal in `nova/definitions.py:6` — and §4's "one atomic receipt writer" for `calibrate/sweep.py`, `catalog/mast_geometry.py` and `imas/mast_parity_gate.py` should extend `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:1187`'s `_write_bytes_at` (with `_publish_directory_no_replace` at line 1197) rather than fork a second writer

findings.reason: the section must state, in its own text, what each new public definition retires or merges, or why it cannot; as written it adds surface and accounts for none of it.
findings.text: §4 `replan-small-primitives` adds five new public definitions (a uniform-axis validator, an array constructor, a receipt writer, a trimmed-string check and a canonical digest) while the section names what it merges only for the duplicated *implementations*, not the added public surface: the counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, and the two "beside" additions retire nothing

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §4 `replan-small-primitives` bundles five unrelated single-function primitives into one node, adding five new surfaces over three different machinery families instead of one deep module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 `replan-gpfs-data-root:84` re-implements path-root resolution rather than extending its owner `nova/database/filepath.py` (`nova/database/filepath.py:110`), and §4's "one atomic receipt writer" duplicates `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:1187` (`_write_bytes_at`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 `replan-small-primitives` adds at least five new public definitions (validator, array constructor, receipt writer, trimmed-string check, digest) and names no retirement or merge in interface-family terms for the two "beside" additions.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes a data-root resolver (§5 `replan-gpfs-data-root`), a receipt-root resolver (§5 `replan-evidence-tooling-paths`) and shared primitives (§4 `replan-small-primitives`) without citing `nova/database/filepath.py` (`FilePath`, `_resolve_absolute`), `nova/definitions.py:6` (`root_dir`), `nova/imas/machine_evidence.py` (`canonical_json`, `require_string`) or `nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:1187` (`_write_bytes_at`), all of which already exist.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the two "beside" items in §4 `replan-small-primitives` would add parallel functions next to `require_string` and `canonical_json` with no statement of why those cannot be extended.
